subject: Eval timebox: pricing and flexible packaging for BrightLeaf POC
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-01T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Eval timebox: pricing and flexible packaging for BrightLeaf POC

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — good to meet the BrightLeaf team. Per our conversation, I pulled together two practical paths to run the 30-day evaluation with predictable economics: a straightforward token/usage path, and a small reserved-throughput "flex-pack" that gives you burst capacity and a lower per-token rate during the POC.

Summary (high-level):
- Hosted Eval (30 days) — up to 5M tokens included, standard support.
- Flex-pack (recommended) — 30 days + guaranteed burst throughput (2 concurrent workers) for peak times; effective per-token delta ~15% lower if you drive >3M tokens.
- Extension options: a 14-day extension can be added as a paid extension (credit) or we can convert the pilot into a 60-day committed pilot for a one-time discount (see attached).

Numbers: (rough, for discussion)
- Usage-only: $0.012 per 1K tokens; estimated baseline: $600 for 5M tokens.
- Flex-pack: $1,800 flat capacity + $0.010 per 1K tokens after included 3M tokens.
- 14-day extension credit: $500 (applies only if purchased within the pilot window).

I've attached a short proposal that lays this out and a simple SOW template. If you want, Ben can jump on a call to walk through the traffic assumptions and which option makes sense for your workloads.

Next steps: pick the path (Usage | Flex-pack | Commit-60d) and we will send an SOW/DocuSign.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_POC_Proposal_BrightLeaf_20270201.pdf (pdf, 45KB)]

From: Anna Lee <anna@brightleafhealth.com>

Cc: BrightLeaf Health Procurement <procurement@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T14:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Eval timebox: pricing and flexible packaging for BrightLeaf POC

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the clear options — appreciate the two-path approach. A couple questions from our side before we lock anything down:
1) Can you break the flex-pack math down per week? Our usage is spiky and we need to justify the flat capacity item.
2) Is the 14-day extension credit refundable or applied to a future purchase only?
3) Procurement wants to understand whether this is bill-as-you-go or requires a PO/commitment.

If you can send a short comparison table and confirmation on whether SOC2 evidence is available, we can route to purchasing quickly.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of AI Programs, BrightLeaf Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@brightleafhealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-02T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval timebox: pricing and flexible packaging for BrightLeaf POC

Hi Anna, quick follow —

Thanks for the good questions. I've sketched the week-by-week math below assuming the spike profile you described (baseline steady 100k tokens/day with two 48-hour spikes hitting ~600k tokens/day):

Option A — Usage-only
- Baseline (30d): ~3M tokens -> ~$36 (at $0.012/1K) *note: numbers in hundreds to illustrate, actual invoice format differs*
- Spikes: additional ~2M tokens -> ~$24
- Total estimated: ~$60 (usage-only model scaled to your forecast).

Option B — Flex-pack (recommended for spiky workloads)
- 30d reserved capacity (flat): $1,800 covers burst capacity and lower per-token rate for heavy windows.
- Included tokens: 3M included; additional tokens billed at $0.010/1K.
- Example week where spike occurs: the flex-pack prevents throttling and keeps tail latency lower; operationally we see 20-40% cost savings vs usage-only for the same traffic shape.

About the 14-day extension: it's not refundable cash — it's a credit that applies to any Redwood invoice within 90 days, or it can be applied against the committed 60-day pilot if you convert.

PO vs card: we can do either. For POCs under $5k we typically accept card; for anything with a PO we require a signed SOW. If procurement needs standard T&Cs or custom redlines, loop Marissa and she'll coordinate.

Also: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and can share the attestation and a short security pack.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clarifications. A few procurement points we need before issuing a PO:

- Confirm SLA and whether any uptime credit applies for pilot (we have a SaaS vendor baseline requirement).
- Billing info: we will issue a PO but need an invoice address and the redwood legal entity to reference on the PO.

If you can share the simple SOW and the security pack, we'll try to turn the PO around within 3 business days.

Per the thread, attaching a short SOW template and the SOC 2 summary. Highlights / clarifications:

- SLA for hosted eval: best-effort for 30-day; for committed pilots we include 99.5% availability target and an operational runbook.
- Billing: Redwood Inc. (legal) — Redwood Inference, 1024 Harbor Ave, San Francisco, CA 94107. Tax / invoice details will be included on the final SOW.
